world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog entry retired and merged into Amdang; look under Amdang (amda1236) instead.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x reference list for Amdang amda1238 (10 entries) and title searches for 'Amdang'/'Biltine' across the Glottolog bibliography (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No phonology, grammar or dictionary entries exist for Amdang beyond Doornbos 1980 (unpublished notes) and Wolf 2010; nothing newer than 2011 with Amdang in the title.
No phonology section; references only Ethnologue, Wolf 2010, Doornbos & Bender 1983, Greenberg 1972, Jungraithmayr 1971 and ethnographic works.

sources.citation: Herce, Borja. 2023. The Typological Diversity of Morphomes: A Cross-Linguistic Study of Unnatural Morphology. Oxford: Oxford University Press (open access, OAPEN 20.500.12657/62891).
sources.note: Nothing on Amdang stress; p.139 remarks on 'the absence of a sufficient description of Amdang, the only other close relative of Fur' (saved as snippet only; located via archive.org full-text search).

sources.citation: Starostin, George. 2011. On Mimi. Journal of Language Relationship / Voprosy jazykovogo rodstva 6: 115-140.
sources.note: Nothing on prosody. Comparative-lexical paper on the two extinct 'Mimi' wordlist languages; explicitly sets aside the 'third Mimi' = Amdang/Biltine as an uncontroversial close relative of Fur and lists the only Amdang data as wordlists (Jungraithmayr 1971; Doornbos in Doornbos & Bender 1983; Wolf 2010), noting that 'proper historical research on the Fur-Amdang group is still seriously impeded by lack of data' (pp.116-117).

sources.citation: Wolf, Katharina. 2010. Une enquête sociolinguistique parmi les Amdang (Mimi) du Tchad: Rapport technique. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2010-028. Dallas: SIL International. 96 pp. (French)
sources.note: No statement on stress, accent or tone anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text for accent/ton/stress/prosod/syllab; only hit for 'accent' is a French-proficiency descriptor, p.23). Sole phonological remark is dialectal [z]~[d] variation (sec. 7.1.1, pp.40-41). Annexe D survey wordlists (pp.70-74, four villages, IPA) and the table on p.41 carry sporadic primary-stress marks, nearly all on the final syllable (e.g. kuˈri 'poule', kɑˈmɑl 'chameau', duguˈdi 'queue', sɪˈmi 'bouche', wɑˈrɑt 'sel'); c. 155 of 160 marked tokens are final-stressed by my count, but c. 90% of polysyllabi…

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Katharina Wolf, SIL Chad survey team). 2007. Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code, Change Request Number 2007-191: retire [miv] Mimi and merge into [amj] Amdang (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International. 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative document. Establishes identity: 'They call themselves Amdang and their language Amdangti. There was no evidence of other Mimi populations and other Mimi dialects.. I suggest collapsing the entries for amj and miv into amj' (p.2).

sources.citation: Jakobi, Angelika. 2002. A grammatical sketch of Amdang. Unpublished manuscript (cited in Wolf 2010:54).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only grammatical description of Amdang known to exist; by a specialist in Fur tonology, so almost certainly contains a phonology section with a tone/stress statement. Would settle whether Amdang is tonal like Fur or has (final?) stress.
